title: Titles show the synopses, artwork and people kept in files beside them
description: Serves PRODUCT.md: "A title's information, artwork and the people in it come from files beside the films" and "Finding something to watch is easy ... artwork and the people in a title". In stage 1 a title has only the name and year from its file name and a poster kept beside it. Octave found a TV home of bare file names hard to browse (#299).
acceptanceCriteria: A title shows the information kept in the files beside it, read automatically as titles are added: its title, original and other titles, year, synopsis, genres and rating, and an episode's own title and synopsis. The design lists the file kinds covered and tests each.
A title shows the artwork kept beside it or in its show's or season's folder (poster, backdrop, logo, a season's and an episode's own picture).
A title lists the people in it with their roles, each with the photo kept beside the files where there is one; where there is none, the app is told so and shows the name alone.
Artwork and people's photos are served without a sign-in at an address that changes when the picture does, and reveal nothing else about the collection (D-20261128-picture-access).
A picture embedded in a film's file is reached only through a link given to a signed-in person's app, which stops working after a stated time (D-20261128-picture-access).
A changed file beside a title is seen at the next scan; a file that can't be read is reported to the operator and holds up nothing else.
The design states the storage and database cost of a collection of 10,000 titles.
notes: From stage 5's artwork and metadata, ordered right after stage 1 because a TV home is mostly titles and artwork (#299). Pages for each person stay in the backlog (BL-20261128-people-pages).
